speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and your tummy looks very big. To understand what is wrong, tell me: does your stool have a bad smell, or have you been vomiting yellow or green fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has your baby passed any stools at all, and if so, were they foul-smelling or containing undigested food? I am also concerned about the tenderness you described; please tell me if you notice any "sausage-shaped" mass in his abdomen when you gently feel him.

speaker: Doctor

That is surprising given the severe distension and tenderness; has your baby been passing gas or any stools at all recently? Did you notice any green (bilious) vomiting episodes?

Please describe what you see on the X-ray or ultrasound images, and tell me the baby's last bowel movement.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyloric Atresia (or severe Hirschsprung's disease requiring surgical exploration given normal imaging but persistent obstruction). 

*Note: While imaging is normal, the clinical picture of an 8-month-old with severe bilious vomiting (if present), feeding intolerance, abdominal distension, and a tender "sausage-shaped" mass is highly suggestive of a mechanical obstruction that may not be visible on standard ultrasound/X-ray (e.g., intestinal atresia or volvulus). Immediate surgical consultation is warranted.*
